paper_sections.title: Differential patterns of cortical activation as a function of fluid reasoning complexity.
fMRI Subject Selection and Behavioral Task
Functional Differences Between High-gfand Low-gf Samples

description.value: The study investigated how cortical activity changes with increasing fluid reasoning complexity in participants with different levels of fluid intelligence, focusing on within-group complexity effects and between-group differences in a fronto-parietal network.

design.value: Two groups selected from the extreme tails of a fluid-intelligence distribution performed moderate and complex reasoning tasks and a control task during fMRI. Brain activity was analyzed within and between the low-gf and high-gf groups using individual-subject GLMs, second-level random-effects analyses, ROI analyses, repeated-measures ANOVA, and between-condition and between-group tests.

task_description.value: A computerized behavioral task composed of 32 fluid reasoning and 32 control problems adapted from the Standard and Advanced Raven Progressive Matrices. Reasoning problems consisted of 3 × 3 matrices with a missing bottom-right entry and eight alternatives; control problems consisted of matrices whose figural elements were devoid of logical relations.

presentation_software.value: E-Prime software, v.1.1, Psychology Software Tools

instructions.value: The subject was instructed to take all the time necessary for generating the solution and when ready to press the button beneath his/her left index finger. During the match period, the participant had to match the generated response with the one suggested by the computer. For control problems, participants were asked to look across the rows and down the columns composing the matrix and then to look at the eight pseudo-alternatives as well. Participants were explicitly taught not to guess the solution and to miss the response when necessary.

stimuli.value: Figural and analytic matrices adapted from the Standard and Advanced Raven Progressive Matrices, plus control matrices with figural elements devoid of logical relations. The reasoning problems were classified according to the number and type of rules governing the relations among stimuli.

task_performance_measures.value: reaction times recorded in the match period

description.value: BOLD contrast functional images were acquired at 1.5 T using T2*-weighted echo planar imaging (EPI) free induction decay (FID) sequences. The acquisition used TR 3,000 ms, TE 60 ms, a 64 × 64 matrix, 256 mm FOV, 4 mm × 4 mm in-plane voxel size, 90° flip angle, 6 mm slice thickness, no gap, and 16 transaxial slices. Functional volumes were acquired in two runs for each functional session, with 146 to 260 volumes per run across subjects.

pulse_sequence_type.value: T2*-weighted echo planar imaging (EPI) free induction decay (FID)

description.value: A high resolution structural volume was acquired at the end of the session via a 3D MPRAGE sequence: sagittal acquisition, 256 × 256 matrix, 256 mm FOV, 1 mm slice thickness, no gap, 1 mm × 1 mm in-plane voxel size, 12° flip angle, TR = 9.7 ms, and TE = 4 ms.

The first three scans of each run were discarded because of T1 saturation effects. Functional scans underwent motion correction, removal of linear trends from voxel time series, coregistration with the corresponding structural data set, transformation into Talairach space, and resampling at 3 mm × 3 mm × 3 mm.

software.value: Brain Voyager QX software (Brain Innovation, The Netherlands)

steps.value: Discard the first three scans of each run because of T1 saturation effects

Inspect estimated translation and rotation parameters for each volume
Remove linear trends from voxel time series
Coregister preprocessed functional volumes with the corresponding structural data set
Transform structural and functional volumes into Talairach space using a piecewise affine and continuous transformation

hrf_model.value: an empirically founded hemodynamic response function

model_settings.value: Correct analytic, error analytic, correct figural, and error figural conditions were predictors of interest. The control task was the baseline, while the instruction and match conditions were predictors of no interest. The boxcar waveform representing the rest and task conditions was convolved with the hemodynamic response function. Temporal autocorrelation was corrected.

model_type.value: second level voxel-wise random effect analysis

model_settings.value: GLM beta values estimated in individual subject analysis were entered into a second level voxel-wise random effect analysis for the whole group (N = 18). Activation maps contrasted correct analytic, error analytic, correct figural, and error figural predictors with the control task, and also contrasted analytic with figural conditions. Maps were thresholded at P < 0.05 corrected for multiple comparisons by the Bonferroni method.

The analysis was performed separately for the low-gf and high-gf groups, considering correct analytic and correct figural predictors against the control task, with a direct contrast between the two groups. Regions of interest were determined from the mask obtained from voxels activated in any condition of interest and group.

A 6 × 2 × 2 × 2 analysis of variance for repeated measures used percent signal change with respect to the control condition as the dependent variable, with ROI, hemisphere, condition, and groups as factors. Results were corrected for multiple comparisons using Bonferroni correction.
For high- and low-IQ volunteers separately, paired sample t-tests compared figural and analytic neural activities recorded in the six ROIs.
A one-way ANOVA between the two groups was performed on the figural BOLD signal recorded in each ROI.
For the high-IQ group, a one-way ANOVA with sex as factor used the individual BOLD responses of each ROI as dependent variables.

description.value: Moderate reasoning problems based on a single rule with perceptually based algorithms, including Constant in a Row or Quantitative Pair-wise Progression.
Complex reasoning problems requiring abstraction of more than one rule or of a single rule based on analytic reasoning, including distribution of three values.

Control problems consisted of 3 × 3 matrices with all entries containing figural elements devoid of any logical relations. Participants were asked to look across the rows and down the columns and then at the eight pseudo-alternatives.
Analytic reasoning trials for which a correct response was given.
Analytic reasoning trials for which an incorrect response was given.
Figural reasoning trials for which a correct response was given.
Figural reasoning trials for which an incorrect response was given.
The instruction “solve” preceded reasoning matrices and “watch” preceded control matrices; each instruction lasted 1,200 ms.
A maximum 1,500-ms period after the reasoning problem in which a red cross overlapped one of the eight alternatives and the participant matched the generated response with the suggested alternative.

interpretations.value: A distributed fronto-parietal network subserving fluid intelligence which is common to moderate and complex reasoning items and is independent from subjects ability level.
